OPC UA: An open industrial communication architecture (IEC 62541) that lets plant machines and IT systems exchange structured data securely across different platforms using TCP port 4840.
middleware: A software layer sitting between the operating system and user programs that handles communication, message passing, and hardware coordination across different robot devices.
non-systematic error: Unpredictable odometry errors caused by external floor interactions, such as wheel slip, floor bumps, or skidding during turns, which vary randomly between runs and cannot be removed by calibration alone.
PROFINET RT: A PROFINET communication class that bypasses standard TCP/IP protocol layers to achieve predictable real-time communication in the 1 to 10 millisecond range.
finite state machine: A system design pattern where a robot stays in exactly one state at a time, switching between defined states when specific sensor events or conditions occur.
L298N: An older dual H-bridge motor driver board that controls two DC motors. Because its internal transistors drop substantial voltage, it produces noticeable heat and needs a large heatsink.
collaborative application: The formal term in ISO 10218:2025 recognizing that safety depends on the entire robotic task, tooling, and workspace, rather than the robot arm alone.
rotation vector: A way to represent 3D orientation where the vector's direction points along the axis of rotation and its length gives the rotation angle in radians, used in URScript poses.
RMW: ROS Middleware, an abstraction layer that connects high-level ROS 2 client libraries to underlying communication systems such as DDS or Zenoh without changing user code.
SLAM: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, the method a mobile robot uses to build a map of an unknown room while tracking its own location inside it.
systematic error: Consistent odometry errors caused by physical robot imperfections, such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty, that repeat identically across runs and can be corrected by software calibration.
lifecycle node: A managed ROS 2 node that moves through explicit states—Unconfigured, Inactive, Active, and Finalized—so a robot system can start up, configure hardware, and shut down safely.
CODE_OF_CONDUCT: A document in a repository that sets ground rules for participant behavior, helping keep discussions constructive, respectful, and welcoming for all community members.
human-in-the-loop: A system design where a human must actively approve each action before the robot executes it, such as a surgeon confirming a cut proposed by a surgical robot.
KAREL: A high-level compiled programming language used on FANUC robot controllers for data handling, file access, and network socket communication alongside everyday teach-pendant motion programs.
QuickMove: An ABB motion control feature that shortens cycle times by automatically calculating the highest safe acceleration and deceleration for the robot at every moment.
program tree: A visual outline in Universal Robots PolyScope that displays robot commands, waypoints, and logic as an expandable list of steps instead of written text code.
service: A two-way communication pattern in ROS where a client node sends a request to a server node and waits for a response, used for quick one-off tasks.
sensor fusion: The process of combining data from multiple different sensors so the resulting estimate of a robot's position or movement has less uncertainty than any single sensor alone.
factory acceptance test (FAT): A formal test of a completed robot cell at the builder's shop before shipment. It checks build quality, wiring, safety interlocks, and basic operation to find problems early.
strobe mode: Pulsing an LED light in brief, intense flashes timed with camera exposure. This reduces heat, extends LED life, and freezes the motion of fast-moving parts on conveyors.
telecentric lens: A specialized optical lens whose chief rays run parallel to the optical axis, maintaining constant image size and eliminating perspective error even as object distance changes.
VDMA 40010: The OPC UA companion specification for robotics that standardizes data models for asset management, condition monitoring, and status across different robot manufacturers.
WSL 2: Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2, a Windows tool that runs a real Linux kernel, allowing developers to install Ubuntu and run ROS tools directly on Windows.
IMU: Inertial Measurement Unit, a sensor package combining accelerometers and gyroscopes (and sometimes magnetometers) to measure a robot's acceleration, turning rate, and orientation.
Arduino Uno: A popular open-source microcontroller board used to prototype robot electronics, available as the classic 8-bit Uno R3 or the faster 32-bit Uno R4.
IEC 61131-3 SFC: Sequential Function Chart, a graphical programming language defined in IEC 61131-3 for industrial PLCs that organizes machine operations into steps, transitions, and action blocks.
Time-Sensitive Networking: A set of IEEE 802 Ethernet standards that provides guaranteed bounded latency, synchronized clocks, and low packet loss for real-time industrial and control traffic.
ISO 10218:2025: The international safety standard for industrial robots, revised in two parts: Part 1 sets requirements for the robot manufacturer, and Part 2 covers integration into cells and applications.
image moments: Weighted calculations of pixel intensities across an image contour used to determine geometric properties such as part area, orientation, and center-of-mass (centroid) coordinates.
ISA/IEC 62443: An international cybersecurity standard series that defines security requirements, risk assessment processes, and zone-based protections for industrial automation and control systems.
assembly: A very low-level programming language where each written command matches a single instruction that the computer's processor runs directly.
action: A ROS communication pattern for long-running tasks that sends periodic progress feedback, can be canceled while running, and returns a final result when complete.
REP 2000: The ROS standard that lists officially supported operating systems, architectures, and platform support tiers for ROS 2 releases.
dimensional gauging: Measuring physical features of a part—such as hole diameters, shaft lengths, or slot widths—by converting camera pixel coordinates into calibrated real-world millimeters.
reinstatement effect: The economic process where new technology creates entirely new jobs and complex tasks for people, such as programming, integrating, and maintaining industrial robot cells.
measurement noise (R): The statistical uncertainty and electrical noise inherent in physical sensor readings, represented by covariance matrix R in a Kalman filter.
black channel principle: A safety networking design where safety and standard messages share unrated cables and switches, placing all error detection and fail-safe diagnostics directly inside the end devices.
Controller Manager: The central component in ros2_control that manages controller lifecycles and connects them to hardware-abstraction interfaces to run the main control loop.
ISO 8373: The international standard that defines robotics terms. Its 2021 edition defines a robot as a programmed, powered machine with some autonomy to move, handle objects, or position tools.
acoustic whine: A high-pitched noise produced when motor windings vibrate from PWM switching frequencies that fall within the audible range of human hearing (20 Hz to 20 kHz).
IO-Link: A standardized point-to-point digital communication technology (IEC 61131-9) connecting industrial sensors and actuators to controllers using standard three-wire cables.
RANSAC: Random Sample Consensus, an algorithm that finds geometric shapes (such as flat tables) in noisy point clouds by repeatedly testing random sample points against a distance threshold to ignore outliers.
automaton: A machine that moves on its own using a built-in mechanism, such as clockwork gears, without sensing or adapting to the world around it (plural: automata).
BiSS: An open, two-way digital communication protocol for absolute encoders that lets a controller read exact shaft positions and exchange configuration or diagnostic data with the encoder.
disparity: The horizontal pixel difference between corresponding points in left and right stereo images. It is inversely proportional to depth, so closer objects produce larger disparity values.
meaningful human control: The principle in robotics ethics and international law requiring human supervision, situational awareness, and the ability to intervene or deactivate autonomous weapons before lethal force is used.
README: The introductory file in an open-source repository that explains what the project does, why it is useful, and how to install and run the code.
simulation-to-reality gap: The difference between a simulated robot in software and its real physical motion, caused by part tolerances, slight fixture misalignments, and mechanical arm deflection.
substitution: A placeholder in a ROS 2 launch file (such as LaunchConfiguration or FindPackageShare) whose actual value is determined only when the launch file runs.
UMBmark: The University of Michigan Benchmark, a calibration test where a robot drives clockwise and counter-clockwise square paths to separate and measure wheel diameter differences and wheelbase errors.
backlighting: A lighting method placing the light source behind an object, producing a sharp black silhouette against a bright background for measuring part outlines and dimensions.
Best Effort: A ROS 2 Quality of Service policy that delivers messages quickly without waiting for acknowledgments or retransmitting lost packets, ideal for high-frequency sensor streams.
PID control: A feedback control loop that calculates corrective motor commands by combining current error, accumulated past error, and the error's rate of change to hold a target speed or position.
robot density: The number of operating industrial robots for every 10,000 factory workers. The International Federation of Robotics uses this measure to compare how automated different countries are.
robtarget: An ABB RAPID data type that defines a complete robot position in millimeters, tool orientation as a quaternion, arm axis configurations, and external axis positions.
underlay: The existing base ROS 2 installation or workspace (such as /opt/ros/lyrical) that an overlay workspace builds upon and relies on for dependencies.
Zenoh: A lightweight communication protocol supported as an alternative middleware in ROS 2, designed with low network overhead for mobile robots and challenging wireless links.
algorithmic bias: Unfair errors or discrimination in machine learning software, often caused by incomplete or unbalanced training data, such as a vision system failing to detect certain pedestrian groups.
fieldbus: An industrial digital network that replaces discrete point-to-point wiring by connecting sensors, actuators, and controllers over a single shared communication cable.
geofencing: Virtual spatial boundaries enforced by software or safety controllers to restrict where a robot or its tool can travel, preventing it from leaving designated safe working zones.
IEEE 7000: An international engineering standard that defines a step-by-step process for identifying ethical concerns, stakeholder values, and privacy risks during system design.
IFR World Robotics: The annual statistical report published by the International Federation of Robotics tracking factory robot installations, operational stock, and robot density across countries worldwide.
MQTT: A lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol running over TCP that lets field devices stream telemetry and status updates to supervisory IT systems.
Quality of Service (QoS): A set of communication rules in ROS 2 that controls how messages are delivered, including reliability, history depth, and whether past messages are saved for new subscribers.
SafeMove: ABB's functional safety monitoring option for robot controllers, running on dedicated safety hardware that monitors positions and speeds independently of the standard controller.
service robot: A robot that performs useful tasks for people or equipment outside industrial factory work, such as cleaning, delivery, inspection, or hospitality.
Transient Local: A ROS 2 Quality of Service setting where the publisher saves past messages so newly connected subscribers receive the latest data immediately, useful for static maps.
conflict of interest: A situation where an engineer's personal, financial, or business interests could bias their professional judgment, or appear to. Ethical codes require engineers to disclose such conflicts promptly.
Data Matrix ECC 200: A 2D matrix barcode with an L-shaped finder pattern that uses Reed-Solomon error correction to read damaged or partially obscured codes.
digital twin: A virtual 3D simulation of a physical robot, cell, and environment used to test, program, and debug operations without stopping the real production line.
node: A single program in ROS that performs one specific job, such as reading a sensor or planning a path, and communicates with other nodes.
Open Source Robotics Alliance: An alliance formed under the Open Source Robotics Foundation in 2024 to guide and support the ongoing development of ROS, Gazebo, and Open-RMF.
brake solenoid: An electromechanical actuator that releases a robot joint's spring-applied holding brake, typically checked and replaced first when troubleshooting brake failure.
cooperative multitasking: A programming approach where tasks share processor time by running brief non-blocking checks against a clock (such as millis()) instead of using blocking delays that freeze the CPU.
Developer Certificate of Origin: A formal declaration that a contributor created the submitted code or has the right to share it under the project's open-source license, confirmed by adding a Signed-off-by line to commits.
ISO/TS 15066: The technical specification that defines maximum force and pressure limits across 29 body areas for safe contact between humans and robots in collaborative applications.
OSHA: Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the US federal agency that enforces workplace safety standards and investigates industrial robot accidents.
RETRY: An ABB RAPID error-handling instruction that re-executes only the specific command that failed, rather than restarting the entire routine.
ROS driver: A software bridge that translates standard ROS messages, topics, and services into the specific network commands required by a robot manufacturer's proprietary controller.
fine calibration: A precision axis recalibration procedure used when robot or external axes lose their stored calibration data, restoring their exact mechanical zero references.
IEEE 802.1AS: The Layer 2 timing and synchronization standard in Time-Sensitive Networking, based on IEEE 1588, that gives all devices on an Ethernet network a shared clock.
magic files: Automated USB backup scripts on Universal Robots controllers that automatically copy programs, installation files, and system configuration as soon as the drive is inserted.
REP 2004: A ROS standard that classifies packages into quality levels based on their testing, documentation completeness, code coverage, and versioning rules.
ROS-Industrial: An open-source initiative and industry consortium that brings ROS and ROS 2 software libraries, standard interfaces, and drivers to factory automation and industrial robot arms.
explicit messaging: Request-reply client-server transactions in EtherNet/IP running over TCP for configuration, parameter changes, and diagnostics on an as-needed basis.
galvanic isolation: The separation of electrical circuits so no direct current flows between them, using components like intermediate relays to block ground loops and noise.
package.xml: The XML manifest file in a ROS package that lists the package name, description, maintainer, software license, and the dependencies needed to build and run it.
foundation model: A large AI model trained on massive amounts of data that can adapt to many tasks. In robotics, vision-language-action models turn camera images and user instructions directly into robot actions.
process noise (Q): The uncertainty in a robot's motion prediction caused by real-world physical disturbances such as wheel slip and uneven terrain, represented by matrix Q in a Kalman filter.
suction cup safety factor: A multiplier (such as 1.5 for smooth parts or 2.0 for porous ones) added to vacuum calculations so a suction cup holds firmly during fast robot movements.
